title: How Iman Gadzhi runs 1M+ registrant launches: mass-market messaging, short-form reach, offers built on objections
summary: Iman Gadzhi explains how his team runs quarterly challenges with 1.2M registrants. He covers speaking to the four audience tiers, using short-form purely for reach to cut ad costs, building offers around objections, and baking in refunds. He also stresses profitability over revenue and building on existing competitive advantages.

principles.text: There are four markets; pick which one you serve. Mass market needs very different language and mindset work than beginners.
principles.quote: There's actually four markets. There's beginner, mid-market, advanced, and then, uh, mass market.

principles.text: Use short-form purely for reach, with no CTAs. Familiarity with your face lowers later ad costs.
principles.quote: Like we have no CTAs in any of our short form ever.

principles.text: Put ego aside and optimize for profit, not vanity revenue.
principles.quote: I think one thing that we've been able to do quite well over the years is put our ego to the side and focus on profitability rather than revenue.

principles.text: Design offers by starting from the buyer's objection, then license or build whatever solves it in advance.
principles.quote: the first thing that we do is we think about what's the objection and then we reverse engineer from there.

principles.text: Evaluate opportunities by your competitive advantages and build an ecosystem around your core, not new unfamiliar domains.
principles.quote: I'm just looking at what are my competitive advantages what are our competitive advantages and like how can I build on that

principles.text: Bake a refund cost into the business and refund generously to avoid complaints and regulator attention.
principles.quote: no matter what business you're in, I would just bake in a get tax where it's like you're you're you're acknowledging that you are being rinsed.
